newsitem.title: UK: Penalties urged for errant cargo airlines.
newsitem.headline: Penalties urged for errant cargo airlines.

text.p: A scheme under which airlines were penalised for failing to provide cargo services promised should be considered by the carriers, the UK Air Freight Forum has recommended.

"What is goose for one is gander for another," said a Forum statement, referring to policies recently implemented by, among others, Air Canada and Emirates that fine agents and shippers who fail to provide promised shipments on time.
The statement recognised that failure to give adequate notice that pre-booked cargo would not in fact arrive gave agents, and especially airlines, major headaches.

"Unfilled space costs airlines dear. To help avoid this regular occurrence, the practice of double-booking space is common among airlines -- a practice which can sometimes backfire resulting in other shippers' cargo being 'bumped'," said the statement.
Imposing penalty charges on the culprits was "one way of focusing the mind", it said.
It added that a similar penalty policy imposed on errant airlines "would help restore some of the confidence lost among shippers and forwarders".
The UK Air Freight Forum comprises 20 leading airlines, forwarders and shippers.
